$comment: Catalog-level UI builder policy for :foundation-catalog, beside its cover sheet. `compose-foundation` is the UI builder's own vocabulary — the containers, the screen frames, the image asset and the shape layers a design is assembled out of — published so `m3-catalog` and `wear-m3-catalog` borrow them from a delivery branch instead of from Kotlin synthesised inside the preview server, which is what makes a fourth catalog cost a release of a repository that has never seen its components. The contract: https://github.com/yschimke/compose-preview-server/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_CATALOG_CONTRACT.md — what this repository owes it: https://github.com/yschimke/compose-ai-tools/blob/main/docs/design/UI_BUILDER_CATALOG_POLICY.md. THE `builtins` BLOCK IS GENERATED by scripts/foundation-catalog.mjs from foundation-catalog/goldens/ and is never edited by hand; everything else here is authored. Nothing reads this file yet — it is authored so what it publishes can be diffed against what the server synthesises today, the same posture this repository's own ui-builder.policy.json was written in. See docs/design/FOUNDATION_CATALOG.md.
$comment_platform: `foundation`, which is a word rather than a platform anyone builds for — and the one declaration in this file that needs reading twice. A platform is compatibility by declared equality: a component pack lands in a catalog whose platform matches, and the New design chooser groups catalogs by the word. This catalog is neither a pack target nor a chooser entry: nothing is DRAWN in `compose-foundation`, it is BORROWED FROM by catalogs that are. Declaring `mobile` would put a second entry in the chooser's Mobile group offering a palette of nothing but containers; declaring the borrowing platform is impossible, because there are two of them. So it declares its own word, and a consumer that shows it to an author has misread it.

wasm.reason: The builder's canvas is Compose Multiplatform for Wasm and links its own Compose, not this catalog's artifacts. The three layout primitives it draws through its own `foundation/*` adapters, which is as close as a box gets to being the same box; the scaffolds and the carousel it draws as placeholders, and says so.

native.reason: The generated Kotlin compiled against this module's own classpath and rendered by Skiko — the same lane that produces this catalog's stickers.

frame.$comment: A rectangle, and no geometry block. This catalog frames nothing: a design is drawn in a BORROWING catalog's frame — a phone screen's device size, a watch's measured round-screen padding — and a frame declared here would be a claim about someone else's screen. `frame` is required by the schema, so it states the neutral answer and the seed device the mobile borrower already uses.

$comment_builtins: All fourteen, and every one of them a builtin — which takes a word of explanation, because the schema's rule is that a component with a call site belongs in the record. Discovery scopes the component record to `material3` / `material` / `wear` library symbols, so `Box`, `Column`, `Row`, the lazy layouts and `Image` do not enter it at all: a per-component @BuilderComponent here attached to nothing and was reported as `component.policy.orphaned`, eleven times, on the first run. The other three — the two scaffolds and the carousel — are Material 3 composables this module deliberately does not render, because drawing them would put `Surface`, `Text` and `TopAppBar` on this catalog's own shelf. So every component of this vocabulary has no call site IN THIS CATALOG'S RECORD, which is exactly the condition a builtin states. The stickers under src/main/kotlin are the PICTURES for this shelf and declare nothing.
$comment_builtinRoles: `role` here is the STRUCTURAL-TEMPLATE role — a closed set of six (`screen-root`, `list`, `list-item`, `overlay`, `controlled`, `decoration`) — and NOT the acceptance role a slot names (`Container`, `Leaf`, `Scaffold`). scripts/foundation-catalog.mjs maps one to the other, and the mapping is lossy in one direction worth stating: a `Box` is not a scrolling list, and `list` is merely the closest of the six for "writes its children in order". The contract sets the test for growing the set — "the test that a new role is general is that two catalogs use it" — and a `container` role is the candidate this catalog is the first evidence for. Nothing reads this file yet, so the mismatch costs nothing today and would cost an export later.

properties.name: containerColor
properties.notes: A colour, written as {"type":"color","value":"#RRGGBB"} or as {"type":"colorToken","value":"primary"} naming one of statusSemantics.colorTokens. A string wrapper, or a role the canvas does not draw, is refused at commit.

properties.name: showByState
properties.notes: Select one child by state. Object fields: selector is a typed scalar or state read; cases is an object mapping child IDs to typed scalar values; optional fallback is a string child ID. Every child must be a case or the fallback. Compose export uses when. Remote export uses StateLayout for non-null number or flag selectors; String equality is unavailable on that target.

properties.name: verticalArrangement
properties.notes: Distribution down the axis. The three aligned values compose with verticalSpacingDp through Arrangement.spacedBy(space, alignment); the three space* values distribute the free space themselves, and Compose has no form that also inserts a fixed gap.

properties.name: alignment
properties.notes: How a parent Box aligns this column. The renderer has always read `alignment` off any Box child and the exporter has always emitted `.align(...)` for it; only the declaration was missing, so a centred column was inexpressible.

properties.name: horizontalArrangement
properties.notes: The Row counterpart of a Column’s verticalArrangement, with the same relationship to horizontalSpacingDp.

properties.name: data
properties.notes: The rows: a `list` value whose entries are `object` values — one dictionary per row, read by the template through `{"type":"binding","value":"<key>"}`, the same reader a component body uses for its arguments.

properties.name: itemSpans
properties.notes: Map stable child id to 'single' or 'full'.

properties.name: assetKey
properties.notes: The key of an asset the canvas can draw, written as {"type":"assetKey","value":"…"}: one of statusSemantics.assetRegistry.keys, or a key pinned in the design's own assets map by PUT /api/ui-builder/v1/designs/{designId}/assets/{assetKey} (raw PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP body) or the ui_builder_put_asset MCP tool. Any other key is refused at commit, so put the picture before inserting the node. A pinned key whose bytes this lane cannot show renders as a placeholder naming it, and exports as Image(painter = ColorPainter(...)) with an ASSET_PLACEHOLDER warning.

$comment_notRemoteCompose: `remote-compose/document`, `/inline` and `/custom` are NOT here, and their absence is a decision. They are seams into Remote Compose — a different library, with `remote-m3` as the catalog that describes it (published from yschimke/wear-m3-catalog's :remote-catalog) — so declaring them here would be this catalog claiming a vocabulary it does not own, which is the exact move `m3-catalog`'s own policy refuses one level up. A borrowing palette still gets them; it gets them from Remote Compose's catalog, or from the packaged fallback until that publishes one.

menu.$comment: The shelves this catalog's components land on in a BORROWING catalog's insert panel, in the order they are reached for: the screen frame first, then what holds things, then the containers, then content, then the decorations. Shelf order matters because an unnamed group sorts after every named one — the failure this repository's own `ui-builder.policy.json` records at length, where twenty-nine shelves ended up alphabetised. The names are the ones the packaged vocabulary already used, so a palette that switches to this catalog does not move every component to a new shelf.

$comment_colorTokens: No `colorTokens`. The roles a design may name belong to the design system it is drawn in — Material 3's for an m3 palette, Wear Material 3's for a watch — and a container borrowed into that palette resolves them against ITS scheme, not against one this catalog would be inventing. Stating a list here would either duplicate `m3-catalog`'s or contradict it.
$comment_code: No `code` block, so the export stays `record`: a call site printed per node from the component record, which is what a catalog of containers needs. The structural templates exist for a screen whose shape no signature carries — a scroll state shared between a scaffold and the list inside it — and the two scaffolds here do not have one yet. They arrive with the template engine rather than ahead of it: templates declared before anything can run them would publish structure nobody has compiled.
